authoredFrom: Erlang semantics plus three corpus adjudications, before this fixture's F3 run. (1) A QUALIFIED type keeps its module: `-record(opts, {env :: cowboy_middleware:env()})` names ONE type, `cowboy_middleware:env` — emitting the bare module atom as a second type name produced 876 stray edges over the 150-file census draw, every one a module masquerading as a type. (2) A module that both DECLARES a callback and DEFINES it (a behaviour with a default implementation; otp/lib/tftp/src/tftp_logger.erl is the corpus witness) yields ONE symbol whose kind is the DEFINITION and whose line is the definition's — the pre-ER3 order dependence left it a Method on the `-callback` line, because the contract is written first. (3) `?MODULE() -> …` is a real function head whose expansion is this module's own atom: the OTP test-suite idiom, 79 corpus sites, each of which previously produced NO symbol at all.
